title: heteroTests Roadmap
text: Corrected Breusch–Pagan / Koenker swap: performBPTest() classical statistic (lmtest::bptest(studentize = FALSE)), performKoenkerTest() studentized n R^2 form (studentize = TRUE); validated machine precision reference-comparison tests. Reimplemented performWildBootstrapTest() null-imposed bootstrap controls size actually power; added size/power regression tests. Kept streaming variants algebraically identical exact counterparts (covered test-streaming.R). Resolved duplicate %||% operator collision abort runHeteroTests() multi-column data. Pass statistical validation matrix (classical regression diagnostics). test checked definition -> reference -> implementation -> numerical equivalence -> size/power. Reference equivalence asserted tests/testthat/test-pass--reference.R; size power measured inst/validation/pass--size-power.R recorded inst/validation/pass--size-power.csv. Corrections: performSzroeterTest() (wrong standardisation, zero power), performNCVTest() (Glejser-type t-test, score test documented), performCookWeisbergTest() (returned Koenker statistic), performHarveyTest() (non-standard auxiliary design statistic). performArchLMTest() performMcLeodLiTest() passed unchanged. Unified input validation across Pass tests; performNCVTest() performCookWeisbergTest() longer bypass shared framework. also removed masking effect unvalidated NCV test succeeded degenerate models acted universal fallback failing tests. compareModelDiagnostics() longer reports substituted fallback diagnostic requested test’s name. Removed two shadowed duplicate definitions: obsolete performHCCovarianceTest() performQuantileRegressionTest() modern_diagnostics.R overwritten load time corrected versions. Correct behaviour depended collation order. Standardised bootstrap permutation p-values finite-simulation convention (1 + #) / (B_eff + 1), regression test covering every resampling entry point.

title: Performance Comparison Guide
text: simulate data two-regressor linear model yi=1+2xi1+3xi2+εi, y_i = 1 + 2 x_{i1} + 3 x_{i2} + \varepsilon_i,  covariates drawn xi1∼𝒩(0,1)x_{i1} \sim \mathcal{N}(0,1) xi2=0.5xi1+uix_{i2} = 0.5 x_{i1} + u_i, ui∼𝒩(0,1)u_i \sim \mathcal{N}(0,1). error variance controlled scenario: Homoskedastic: εi∼𝒩(0,1)\varepsilon_i \sim \mathcal{N}(0, 1) Linear heteroskedasticity: εi∼𝒩(0,(1+1.5|xi1|)2)\varepsilon_i \sim \mathcal{N}\left(0, (1 + 1.5 |x_{i1}|)^2\right) Clustered heteroskedasticity: probability 0.5 observation enters high-variance regime 𝒩(0,2.52)\mathcal{N}(0, 2.5^2), otherwise remains 𝒩(0,12)\mathcal{N}(0, 1^2) avoid simulation failures wrap diagnostic safe helper returns NA input requirements met. repeat scenario 200 times estimate rejection frequencies 5% level.
code: generate_sample <- function(n = 180, scenario = c("homoskedastic", "linear", "clustered")) {   scenario <- match.arg(scenario)   x1 <- rnorm(n)   x2 <- 0.5 * x1 + rnorm(n)   if (scenario == "homoskedastic") {     errors <- rnorm(n, sd = 1)   } else if (scenario == "linear") {     errors <- rnorm(n, sd = 1 + 1.5 * abs(x1))   } else {     regime <- rbinom(n, 1, 0.5)     sds <- ifelse(regime == 1, 2.5, 1)     errors <- rnorm(n, sd = sds)   }   y <- 1 + 2 * x1 + 3 * x2 + errors   data.frame(y = y, x1 = x1, x2 = x2) } safe_pvalue <- function(fn) {   res <- tryCatch(fn(), error = function(e) NULL)   if (is.null(res) || is.null(res$p.value)) {     NA_real_   } else {     res$p.value   } }  run_diagnostics_once <- function(data) {   model <- lm(y ~ x1 + x2, data = data)   c(     white = safe_pvalue(function() performWhiteTest(model, data)),     breusch_pagan = safe_pvalue(function() performBPTest(model, data)),     koenker = safe_pvalue(function() performKoenkerTest(model, data)),     harvey = safe_pvalue(function() performHarveyTest(model))   ) } run_simulation <- function(scenario, reps = 200) {   replicate(reps, run_diagnostics_once(generate_sample(scenario = scenario)), simplify = "matrix") }  calc_rejection_rate <- function(result_matrix, alpha = 0.05) {   rowMeans(result_matrix < alpha, na.rm = TRUE) }

using df = 5. #> [INFO] White test completed: statistic = 6.4178 df = 5 p = 0.2677 bp_engineering <- safe_htest(   function() performBPTest(engineering_model, diagnostic_ext),   "Breusch-Pagan test" ) #> [INFO] Running Breusch-Pagan test koenker_engineering <- safe_htest(   function() performKoenkerTest(engineering_model, diagnostic_ext),   "Koenker test" ) #> [INFO] Running Koenker test harvey_engineering <- safe_htest(   function() performHarveyTest(engineering_model),   "Harvey test" ) #> [INFO] Running Harvey test engineer_tests <- list(   white = white_engineering,   breusch_pagan = bp_engineering,   koenker = koenker_engineering,   harvey = harvey_engineering ) engineer_tests #> $white #>  #>  White's test for heteroscedasticity #>  #> data:  engineering_model #> X-squared = 6.4178, df = 5, p-value = 0.2677 #> alternative hypothesis: heteroscedasticity present #>  #>  #> $breusch_pagan #>  #>  Breusch-Pagan test for heteroscedasticity #>  #> data:  y ~ x1 + x1_sq + x2 #> X-squared = 2.65, df = 3, p-value = 0.4488 #>  #>  #> $koenker #>  #>  Koenker studentized Breusch-Pagan test #>  #> data:  y ~ x1 + x1_sq + x2 #> X-squared = 2.9548, df = 3, p-value = 0.3986 #>  #>  #> $harvey #>  #>  Harvey test for multiplicative heteroscedasticity #>  #> data:  y ~ x1 + x1_sq + x2; variance regressors: model regressors #> X-squared = 1.9025, df = 3, p-value = 0.5929 #> alternative hypothesis: error variance is a multiplicative function of the variance regressors engineer_results$vif #>         x1      x1_sq         x2  #> 102.975949   1.011998 102.854968 engineer_results$reset #>  #>  RESET test for nonlinearity #>  #> data:  y ~ x1 + x1_sq + x2 #> F = 1.336, df1 = 2, df2 = 144, p-value = 0.2661 pvals <- sapply(engineer_tests, function(x) x$p.value) pval_df <- data.frame(   test = names(pvals),   p_value = as.numeric(pvals) )  ggplot(pval_df, aes(x = reorder(test, p_value), y = p_value)) +   geom_col(fill = "#0072B2", alpha = 0.8) +   geom_hline(yintercept = 0.05, linetype = "dashed", colour = "#D55E00") +   coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 1)) +   coord_flip() +   labs(     x = "Test",     y = "p-value",     title = "Contrasting heteroscedasticity diagnostics"   ) +   theme_minimal() #> Coordinate system already present. #> ℹ Adding new coordinate system, which will replace the existing one.

title: Heteroscedasticity Diagnostics for Linear Models
text: heteroTests implements broad collection heteroscedasticity diagnostics linear models R. includes classic tests White, Breusch–Pagan Goldfeld–Quandt along helper functions visualise mitigate heteroscedasticity. Maintained Diogo Ribeiro (dfr@esmad.ipp.pt, ORCID 0009-0001-2022-7072) Faculty Media Arts Design, Technical University Porto.

title: Heteroscedasticity Diagnostics for Linear Models
text: Every test returns base-R htest object follows perform*Test(model, data, ...) convention, results print, subset compose like stats::bptest() slot directly automated pipelines. Auxiliary-regression tests — White, classical Breusch–Pagan, Koenker (studentized), Harvey, Park, Glejser. classical studentized Breusch–Pagan statistics validated lmtest::bptest() machine precision. Group-wise variance tests — Levene, Brown–Forsythe, Bartlett, Fligner–Killeen, Hartley’s F-max (validated car). Rank-based non-constant-variance diagnostics — Spearman, Cameron–Trivedi, Cook–Weisberg NCV, spread–level. ARCH-type tests time series — Engle’s ARCH LM McLeod–Li. Modern resampling robust diagnostics — null-imposed wild bootstrap, HC0–HC4 covariance test, quantile-regression test, rank-permutation test, high-dimensional spatial variants settings classical asymptotics unreliable. Scalability — streaming implementations (performWhiteTestStreaming(), performBPTestStreaming(), performKoenkerTestStreaming()) accumulate auxiliary cross-products chunks; results exact memory-bounded, runHeteroTests() adopts automatically large inputs. Remediation guidance — weighted least squares (fitWLS()), robust fits (fitRobust()), variance-stabilising transforms (autoTransform()), model-comparison helper, recommendation engine (generateHeteroRecommendations()) interprets diagnostic run. Ecosystem integration — broom tidiers, ggplot2 theming/autoplot, helpers tidymodels, survey designs grouped pipelines.

title: Perform Harvey test for multiplicative heteroscedasticity — performHarveyTest
text: Harvey (1976) models error variance \(\sigma_i^2 = \exp(z_i^\top \gamma)\) tests \(\gamma = 0\) auxiliary regression \(\log \hat{e}_i^2\) \(z_i\). null auxiliary error behaves like centred \(\log \chi^2_1\) variate variance \(\pi^2 / 2 \approx 4.9348\), classical statistic \(\mathrm{ESS} / (\pi^2 / 2)\), asymptotically chi-square \(q\) degrees freedom. Setting studentize = TRUE replaces fixed constant \(\pi^2 / 2\) auxiliary residual mean square refers overall F statistic F distribution. two forms asymptotically equivalent normal errors; studentized form reliable normality doubtful, \(\pi^2 / 2\) null variance \(\log \hat{e}^2\) Gaussian errors. Degrees freedom taken realised rank auxiliary design, rank-deficient variance model credited degrees freedom aliased columns.

"fitted" uses fitted values square, behaviour releases 0.7.0. studentize logical; FALSE (default) chi-square statistic \(\mathrm{ESS} / (\pi^2 / 2)\) reported, otherwise auxiliary regression F statistic.

title: Szroeter test for ordered alternatives — performSzroeterTest
text: ordering residuals \(\hat{e}_{()}\) order_by, test forms rank-weighted average squared residuals $$h = \frac{\sum_{= 1}^n \, \hat{e}_{()}^2}{\sum_{= 1}^n \hat{e}_{()}^2},$$ Szroeter's (1978) class statistics evaluated canonical weights \(h_i = \). homoskedasticity \(h\) centred mean rank \((n + 1) / 2\) variance \((n^2 - 1) / (6n)\), $$Q = \frac{h - (n + 1) / 2}{\sqrt{(n^2 - 1) / (6n)}}$$ asymptotically standard normal. Variance grows order_by shifts weight onto high ranks drives \(Q\) upwards. implementation relies package validation helpers align supplied data model residuals, check ordering variable present, ensure sufficient sample size variability squared residuals.

Larger values yield smoother p-value estimates cost additional runtime. parallel Logical scalar; TRUE bootstrap loop executed parallel::mclapply() parallel package forked processing available.

text: htest object reporting asymptotic White statistic bootstrap p-value. returned object also stores simulated test statistics boot_statistics inspection.

title: Bootstrap White test — performWhiteTestBootstrap
text: fitted model \(\hat{y} = X\hat{\beta}\), algorithm proceeds follows: Compute White's LM statistic \(n R^2\) auxiliary regression squares cross-products regressors. Generate \(B\) bootstrap samples resampling centred residuals replacement, forming \(y^{*(b)} = \hat{y} + \hat{e}^{*(b)}\). Refit model bootstrap sample recompute White's statistic \(T^{*(b)}\) using auxiliary specification. Estimate bootstrap p-value \(\hat{p} = B^{-1} \sum_{b = 1}^B \{T^{*(b)} \ge T_{\text{obs}}\}\). bootstrap distribution offers improved size control moderate sample sizes high-dimensional designs chi-squared approximation may inaccurate. parallel = TRUE resampling step exploits available CPU cores reduce computation time.

title: Memory-efficient White test for large datasets — performWhiteTestStreaming
text: Computes White's statistic via chunked cross-products rather fitting full auxiliary regression memory. streaming approach allows test scale datasets otherwise exhaust available RAM.

title: Memory-efficient White test for large datasets — performWhiteTestStreaming
text: model fitted stats::lm object representing mean specification diagnosed. data base::data.frame (object coercible one) containing variables referenced model. must include observations used fit model checked missing values. chunk_size Positive integer specifying number observations per chunk. Smaller values reduce memory usage expense additional iteration overhead. cross_products Logical scalar indicating whether include pairwise cross-products regressors auxiliary regression. Defaults TRUE remain enabled unless dimensionality makes regression unstable. max_interactions Single positive integer giving maximum number original predictors cross-products generated. number regressors exceeds threshold, cross-products dropped avoid explosive growth columns. Defaults 10. progress Logical flag indicating whether progress bar displayed streaming data. Defaults interactive().

title: Memory-efficient White test for large datasets — performWhiteTestStreaming
text: htest object containing chi-squared statistic, p-value, metadata chunked computation.

title: Memory-efficient White test for large datasets — performWhiteTestStreaming
text: streaming implementation iteratively builds cross-product matrices required auxiliary regression without materialising full design matrix. chunk contributes \(X'X\), \(X'y\), summary statistics response. final \(n R^2\) statistic computed exactly standard White test, ensuring numerical equivalence dramatically reducing peak memory usage. Matrix installed, sparse cross-products leveraged automatically large chunks.

title: Memory-efficient White test for large datasets — performWhiteTestStreaming

title: Wild bootstrap heteroscedasticity test — performWildBootstrapTest
text: Calibrates Breusch-Pagan Lagrange multiplier statistic null-imposed wild bootstrap, providing p-value accurate small samples non-normal errors without relying asymptotic \(\chi^2\) approximation.

title: Wild bootstrap heteroscedasticity test — performWildBootstrapTest
code: performWildBootstrapTest(   model,   data,   B = 499,   distribution = c("rademacher", "mammen"),   progress = interactive() )

title: Wild bootstrap heteroscedasticity test — performWildBootstrapTest
text: model fitted stats::lm object describing mean structure whose residual variance assessed. data base::data.frame (compatible object) containing variables referenced model. data must include observations used fit model contain unresolved missing values. B Integer number bootstrap replications. Defaults 499. distribution Multiplier distribution used wild perturbation. Supported options "rademacher" "mammen". progress Logical flag controlling whether progress reported running bootstrap loop.

title: Wild bootstrap heteroscedasticity test — performWildBootstrapTest
text: object class htest containing observed Breusch-Pagan statistic, bootstrap p-value, additional details bootstrap element.

title: Wild bootstrap heteroscedasticity test — performWildBootstrapTest
text: observed statistic usual \(n R^2\) auxiliary regression squared residuals regressors. bootstrap reference distribution, however, must generated homoscedastic null — otherwise inherits heteroscedasticity test looking procedure loses power. bootstrap sample therefore built leverage-standardised, mean-centred residuals \(r_i = e_i/\sqrt{1-h_{ii}}\) (common variance \(H_0\)) resampled ..d. perturbed wild multiplier \(v_i\), \(y_i^* = \hat y_i + r^*_i v_i\). statistic recomputed refit p-value \((1 + \#\{T_b^* \ge T\})/(B + 1)\). \(H_0\) controls size even heavy-tailed errors; alternative observed statistic extreme relative homoscedastic reference, giving power.

title: Wild bootstrap heteroscedasticity test — performWildBootstrapTest
text: Davidson, R., & Flachaire, E. (2008). wild bootstrap, tamed last. Journal Econometrics, 146(1), 162–169. Godfrey, L. G. (2006). Tests regression models heteroskedasticity unknown form. Computational Statistics & Data Analysis, 50(10), 2715–2733. Wu, C. F. J. (1986). Jackknife, bootstrap resampling methods regression analysis. Annals Statistics, 14(4), 1261–1295.

title: Bootstrap a test statistic — rbootstrap_test_statistic
text: resample argument decides replicates mean. resample = "null" (default) response regenerated \(\hat y_i + e^*_i\), \(e^*_i\) drawn replacement model's residuals dividing \(\sqrt{1 - h_i}\) centring. data satisfy homoscedasticity construction, replicates estimate null distribution p_value test. leverage correction matters: OLS residuals variance \(\sigma^2 (1 - h_i)\), resampling unscaled -disperses regenerated errors, inflates rejection rate. resample = "pairs" rows sampled replacement. replicates follow statistic's distribution whatever variance structure data actually , useful describing variability null distribution: replicates centred observed statistic, comparing two returns roughly 0.5 whatever data. Measured rejection \(\sigma_i = x_i^2\) 0%. p_value therefore NA pairs resampling. Neither strategy accepts glm: replicate refitted least squares, family link discarded replicates describe different model one supplied. Null-imposed resampling additionally requires response plain variable. log(y) ~ x fitted values log scale data column holds y, regenerating one refitting take logarithm twice. case raises error; resample = "pairs" resamples rows unaffected .

title: Bootstrap a test statistic — rbootstrap_test_statistic
text: test_function function accepts (model, data, ...) returns object numeric statistic element (typically htest result). model fitted model class lm. glm rejected: replicate refitted least squares, discard family link. data Data frame used fitting model. B Integer, number bootstrap replications. Defaults 1000. parallel Logical, compute replicates parallel possible? ci_level Confidence level percentile interval. resample Bootstrap strategy. "null" (default) regenerates response homoscedasticity yields testable p_value; "pairs" samples rows data replacement yields replicates interval p-value. See Details. n_cores Optional integer specifying number worker processes use parallel = TRUE. Defaults parallel::detectCores() - 1. progress Logical flag controlling whether textual progress bar displayed bootstrap replication. ... Additional arguments forwarded test_function.

title: Bootstrap a test statistic — rbootstrap_test_statistic
text: list components: original Result returned test_function original data. original_statistic Numeric value test statistic original sample. replicates Numeric vector bootstrap statistics. ci Percentile interval bootstrap distribution statistic, ci_level. summarises resampled statistic falls; confidence interval parameter carries coverage guarantee. p_value Empirical p-value null-imposed replicates, computed \((1 + \#\{T^*_b \ge T\}) / (B_{\mathrm{eff}} + 1)\); NA resample = "pairs". B Requested number replications. effective_samples Number non-missing bootstrap replications. call Matched call reproducibility.
